# COR092 `missing-end-label`

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

The `end` statement of a named construct does not repeat the construct name.

## Why

When a construct has a name (`outer: do`), the standard requires its `end` statement to repeat it
(`end do outer`); compilers reject the code otherwise. Reported here so the error shows up with the
other findings, before a build.

## Reported

```fortran
outer: do i = 1, n
end do
```

## Preferred

```fortran
outer: do i = 1, n
end do outer
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR092] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR092` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C143` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
